meta.storyTitle: Track long-running work consistently across executors

override.reason: User approved revision 3 of the presented s1 LLD with an explicit override after the second independent review. Two medium design findings remain: specify how the daemon verifies the originating conversation on an ordinary launching connection before issuing its first observation grant, and add explicit tests distinguishing measured phase/count advancement from duplicate samples, reads and heartbeats. The earlier bounded-recovery finding was carried forward because the reviewer could not inspect the rendered S001 sequence diagram. The user directed that diagram validation be skipped. Preserve these design findings as implementation verification requirements.

summary.prose: The daemon foundation keeps each task tied to its verified executor and originating conversation. It stores bounded observations, exposes one authorized snapshot model, and recovers state after restart. Executor activity and optional polling run on separate schedules.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Use executor delegates with a shared daemon coordinator. Preserve legacy workflow and analyze IPC frames and existing execution authority. The coordinator feeds a typed VS Code adapter, request-scoped MCP notifications and one optional fallback observation schedule.

ownedContracts.name: Task identity and delegate observation
ownedContracts.purpose: One verified owner binds each task attempt to one project and originating invocation. An insrc chat may own many invocations, and an invocation may launch many tasks. Each task has one current attempt, with at most one active owner epoch. External host, daemon session and extension chat identities are optional distinct bindings, never inferred from one another. Both delivery paths use this delegate snapshot. The foundation is parameterized by producer-owned detail types, so it has no type dependency on later stories.

ownedContracts.name: Scoped snapshots, subscriptions and observation control
ownedContracts.purpose: The daemon authorizes every operation against server-verified caller/project/origin bindings, including logs and controls. A read yields a compact snapshot, meaningful-change indicator and revision cursor. Observer loss, executor state and session retention are independent. The shared coordinator arbitrates one optional fallback schedule per task, independent of all native subscriptions. Owner credentials, internal session identifiers and fencing fields remain server-side. A structured fallback lease governs the scheduler, without granting execution authority.

ownedContracts.name: Execution-owned activity and chat retention
ownedContracts.purpose: One current owned attempt may hold at most one active association for its originating insrc conversation. Each chat may have many associations. The coordinator renews through verified executor activity, and the actual session owner consumes the lease or a runtime renewal. View closure does not release a retained conversation. Removing a conversation releases only its association and retains project-scoped authorized task results.

boundary.internal: Own daemon coordination, verified registration, cursors, normalization, scoped read/subscribe/control, durable state, owner fencing and fallback schedule arbitration. Keep storage, fencing and expiry implementation private.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Own adapters for existing workflow and analyze producer signals and terminal/owner evidence. Existing stream shape and command semantics remain compatible.
Own DesignReviewDelegate and CodeReviewDelegate and mappings from checkpoint progress and execution ownership. Review results, admission, retries and publication remain under the existing engines.
Own TestDelegate and managed reporter interpretation, including suite/case identity, provisional counts and abnormal exit. Keep test orchestration and exit semantics unchanged.

Own typed VS Code reader and transcript row, current status projection and bindings to the session owner. Render durable snapshots by origin across turns and multiple windows without executing or polling models.
Own MCP adapter, capability qualification, explicit opt-in disclosure and connection to the coordinator's fallback lease. No vendor-specific process changes or assumptions about session identity.

nonFunctional.performance: Proposed caps for qualification are one coalesced active snapshot per second per task, 8 KiB per snapshot, 32 retained meaningful milestones, 16 queued observer updates and a reserved terminal state. Enforce per-project limits of 128 tracked active observations and 1,024 retained terminal observations, plus a global disk budget of 128 MiB. Exceeding observation capacity must report degradation without refusing, cancelling or slowing work. Terminal updates bypass normal coalescing. Reserve the observation terminal slot and bounded storage on admission. Evict only older terminal entries by policy, and refuse new observation with a capacity state when no reservation is possible. Do not evict active owners to admit new observations.
nonFunctional.security: Authenticate observations via existing daemon caller identity and verify project, conversation/invocation and task attempt before returning any snapshot, detail or control. Opaque cursors and task IDs do not grant authorization. Persist and expose sanitized structured measurements only. Detailed logs remain authorized, bounded references. No direct database access in MCP or VS Code.
nonFunctional.observability: Measure emitted and coalesced progress, cursor gaps, scheduler degradation, stale source age, rejected owner fences and retention transitions separately. Qualify each producer end to end, verify zero extra model invocations for native paths, and live-qualify CLI token, rendering, background lifetime and scheduling per version/session. Never log raw prompts, output or credentials as progress.
nonFunctional.durability: Use daemon-owned atomic per-task snapshots on local storage, with bounded milestone records and terminal result pointers. Persist terminal state before delivery. Refresh verified owner activity every 30 seconds with a 120-second lease, qualifying the margin against the actual session owner's idle threshold. After daemon restart recover persisted observations before accepting new owner events. Hold stale owner retention at most through its bounded grace and show interrupted or unknown until authority is reverified. Terminal retention is seven days subject to bounded capacity, after which separately available executor results remain authoritative. For executors without durable result history, expiry is explicit and is never rendered as a success, cancellation or new execution.

api.name: TaskProgressDelegate

parameters.name: task
parameters.purpose: Server-issued project, invocation, task and attempt tuple.

errors.condition: Measurement fails validation or source is unreachable.
Owner handle, current attempt, epoch or authoritative sequence does not match.
Capacity, bad origin, conflicting admission or expired recovery record.

preconditions: Bind a delegate and runtime-only owner handle to the registered invocation before detaching.

The daemon execution host alone supplies opaque TrustedLaunch, TrustedRetry and TrustedSurvival values through an in-process port. None are deserialized from IPC. TrustedLaunch binds the registered project, an already verified origin and a server-issued invocation. The producer key is stable only inside that invocation.

A daemon composition root registers one producer port per ProgressKind with a strict validator and projection of its detail schema and, where supported, a cancellation hook. The coordinator rejects duplicate registration for a different port. Concrete owner adapters remain in s2–s4.

A next attempt requires an explicit trusted executor retry decision and either a verified terminal predecessor or authority revoked before rollover. Revalidation requires evidence from the actual execution owner of the same surviving or resumed attempt. A client reconnect or a producer-supplied identifier is insufficient.
postconditions: No execution, model, cancellation or lease side effects.
Read results are revalidated against current attempt and epoch after await.

Successful admission commits identity and reservation before returning a daemon-created runtime-only owner handle. Matching duplicate admission returns the same handle while it remains current. Conflicting replay refuses without altering the original.

Lifecycle, measurement signals and renewals use one owner-scoped monotonically increasing sequence. The host checks the opaque handle, attempt and epoch before every mutation. Duplicate identical lifecycle evidence is idempotent, conflicting equal-sequence evidence is rejected, and terminal state is immutable.

Lifecycle evidence supplies authoritative state independently of progress measurements. A terminal outcome includes verified executor disposition and an optional result locator resolved to a scoped opaque reference. The coordinator validates outcome kind and commits before delivery. No delegate read creates a terminal outcome.

Refresh signalling is coalesced. Capture a refresh generation, then recheck current owner, attempt, lifecycle and measurement revision after asynchronous progress(). A heartbeat does not invalidate a valid newer measurement from the same owner, but an old refresh cannot overwrite one already accepted.

The cancellation hook receives an idempotency key and the current owner handle. Acceptance means request received. Verified terminal evidence alone establishes cancellation. The coordinator never dispatches a stored pending request on restart.

api.name: ProgressSnapshot

parameters.name: task
parameters.purpose: Task identity looked up through the caller’s authorized binding.

returns.meaning: One validated projection shared by reads and subscriptions.

errors.condition: Missing, expired, revoked or wrong-purpose grant, or a different socket used the binding. Return the same task-unavailable response externally.

preconditions: IPC handler validates server-bound peer/session/project, capability and origin tuple. A matching request tuple alone grants nothing.

IPC dispatch creates connection identity from the accepted socket. The daemon execution host creates or resolves the originating invocation through an authorized launch and the registry’s canonical project identity. Caller-supplied cwd, labels, PIDs, chat IDs and task tuples are selectors only. An unbound ordinary IPC caller cannot mint or renew a grant.

The coordinator issues an opaque random 256-bit scoped grant only to the trusted launching connection or a verified adapter acting for that invocation. Store only its digest, task/attempt, purpose, allowed operations, expiry and revocation generation in daemon-owned state. Deliver the secret on the authorized transport and keep it out of logs, snapshots, cursors and model input. Clients retain it only in their trusted runtime or existing secure storage.
postconditions: Public snapshot omits internal owner, epoch, transport credentials, session IDs and raw log paths.
Cursor covers snapshot order while measurement revision covers progress change. Heartbeat, as-of reads and reconnect do not increment measurement revision.

The attach handler checks the grant against the durable digest and generation, registered project, requested purpose, current attempt and expiry, then binds the observer to the current TrustedRpcContext connection identity. Each read, subscription, scheduler operation and control rechecks that binding and permission. Disconnect removes the live binding. Reconnect or daemon restart requires presenting the still-valid grant again and receives a new binding. Cursor alone never authenticates.

The trusted execution host or authorized owner of the corresponding conversation can revoke the grant. Revoke durably before acknowledgement, invalidate bindings and pending delivery, and terminate the matching subscription. Registry removal invalidates all grants for that project. Prior-attempt grants cannot observe or cancel a replacement attempt.

Issue the separate task-scoped project-history grant to the trusted originating project adapter at admission, with observe/details only and a bounded retention expiry. Conversation removal revokes conversation-scoped grants and releases only their associations. The project-history holder can reattach to surviving task state after removal, with no conversation access, lease renewal or cancellation. A bare registered project path never authorizes browsing another task.

Attempt rollover issues fresh grants only to the verified origin adapter. The adapter can update the same stable task row after authorized reattachment. No prior-attempt grant can follow the rollover by itself.

api.name: ObservationReply

parameters.name: observer
parameters.purpose: Server-owned transport association and explicit fallback opt-in.

returns.meaning: Typed reply with compact details, change state and optional schedule hint.

errors.condition: Client has no scheduler or fallback lease is not owned.
Another bound holder owns the current unexpired scheduler generation.
Wrong holder, stale generation, revoked binding or expired scheduler lease.
Current monotonic time precedes the next eligible cadence slot.
An accepted slot has not settled or reached its deadline.
No healthy authorized scheduler can claim this slot.

preconditions: For fallback, coordinator admits one fenced lease per stable task. Subscribers without the lease can read the cached shared view but cannot claim a poll slot.

A bound observer needs explicit opt-in, the fallback permission and a verified scheduler capability. The coordinator issues a lease to one connection-bound holder. Claim and renew are atomic against that stable task. Lease and slot generations are allocated by the daemon, never chosen by the caller.
postconditions: Initial snapshot then one slot each 60 seconds on monotonic cadence, with no overlapping calls or catch-up bursts. Use wall time only for guidance. Transfer retains anchor, watermark and cursor. On process restart suspend fallback until fresh authorized opt-in and ownership are verified.
Replay serves cached last result. Unknown/foreign cursor cannot read another task; an expired authorized cursor receives resync.

Initial claim returns the existing current snapshot through read and sets a monotonic cadence anchor if absent. The scheduler lease lasts 120 seconds and is renewed by the holder at or before each healthy 60-second slot. Disconnect, explicit release, expiry, revocation or terminal state revokes its generation. A successor receives the existing anchor, last consumed slot and observation cursor. Transfer does not emit another scheduled poll.

A poll atomically claims the current slot or returns too-early, slot-in-flight or a cached response for an already completed slot. Each in-flight slot holds the lease generation and a deadline before the next cadence boundary. Deadline or revoke cancels its observation signal. Finalization rechecks the live generation and slot before updating the cached response or watermark. A late completion returns stale-lease without delivery, cursor advance or task mutation.

While a revoked slot is still draining, keep its bounded in-flight reservation until it settles or reaches its deadline. A replacement holder uses the next eligible slot after that reservation, skipping unavailable slots. Retain the consumed watermark across handoff. Suspension reports its cause and next eligible time; recovery resumes anchored 60-second slots without catch-up. Terminal transition revokes the scheduler and closes further polling with the authorized cached terminal snapshot.

A cached slot reply is scoped to its authorized task, attempt and scheduler generation. Use the requesting binding and cursor to derive changed, unchanged or resync from the cached projection. No replay invokes progress() again.

api.name: ObservationControl
api.signature: interface ObservationControl { readonly task: TaskRef; readonly action: 'stop-observation' | 'cancel-execution'; readonly requestId: string; }

parameters.name: request
parameters.purpose: Explicit user-derived action with bounded idempotency key.

returns.meaning: Observation detached, cancellation requested or unsupported.

errors.condition: Same scoped request ID with different action or attempt.
Caller lacks target or action authorization.

preconditions: Stop observation is scoped to the caller’s observer and releases its fallback lease. Cancel requires current attempt, supported control and executor cancellation capability.
postconditions: Persist cancel-pending before dispatch, key by task/attempt/requestId, and require idempotent owner request. Replays return the durable pending/outcome without a second dispatch. Restart surfaces pending for owner reconciliation and never replays it automatically.
Only verified termination can become cancelled. A race with normal completion keeps the executor’s verified terminal outcome.

api.name: TaskActivityLease
api.signature: interface TaskActivityLease { readonly task: TaskRef; readonly origin: TaskOrigin; readonly fence: TaskOwnerFence; readonly renewedAt: string; readonly expiresAt: string; }

parameters.name: event
parameters.purpose: Runtime-only owner handle, matching epoch and strictly advancing owner sequence.

returns.meaning: One live association with the verified conversation, or none for an unbound task.

errors.condition: Expired epoch, stale sequence or terminal attempt.

preconditions: Admission verifies originating association before detach. A replacement owner proves the executor still owns or actually resumed the execution.
postconditions: Runtime renewal every 30 seconds, lease expiry at 120 seconds; use monotonic time in process. No observer can grant activity or renew a lease. Release affects only this attempt.

dataModelChanges.details: One registered project owns many invocation scopes. A verified invocation owns zero or more tasks. A task owns one current attempt and zero or more retained prior attempt summaries, and an attempt has at most one verified live owner epoch. The optional conversation binding belongs to one invocation and identifies one insrc conversation, which can own many invocations. Native and daemon session IDs are separately verified bindings and remain private. Reserve a fixed encoded record budget before returning observation admitted. Serialize mutations per stable task and arbitrate the reservation ledger globally, outside the per-task lock; never await delegate reads, transport sends or process cancellation under the lock. Reject unmatched duplicate registrations and make exact same-owner replays idempotent.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: Versioned envelope: trusted origin, stable task key, current attempt and epoch, owner watermark, snapshot revision and meaningful revision, latest bounded snapshot, prior attempt summaries, terminal pointer and cancellation receipt.

dataModelChanges.details: Daemon-only directory under its state root, keyed by a hash of trusted project, invocation and task. Use mode 0700 on the directory and 0600 files, reject symlinks, use an exclusive temporary file on the same filesystem, flush file then rename then flush the directory before acknowledging durable transitions. Reuse the existing atomic-replacement pattern where it provides those guarantees, and add the missing flush and security steps at this boundary. Active state and milestones coalesce at one update per second per task, while owner admission, attempt rollover and terminal snapshots commit before publication. Compact snapshots to 8 KiB, cap milestones and prior summaries at 32 total, cap observer queues at 16 and reserve a terminal slot. Reserve enough disk for atomic replacement, cap 128 active and 1,024 retained terminal observations per project and 128 MiB globally. At capacity, evict eligible terminal records only and otherwise refuse observation visibly. Executor work continues. Terminal retention is seven days subject to bounded capacity. Persist neither raw reporter output nor unvalidated labels. Validate version, bounds and owner identity before adoption; quarantine corrupt records within the storage budget. On startup or verified owner loss, transfer unrevalidated work to a recovery state for at most 120 seconds from the first durable owner-loss timestamp. Preserve that original deadline across restarts. During grace it retains the original reservation. At expiry, persist an explicit unknown/expired observation tombstone, drop detailed payload and invalidate owner and live-observer credentials. A still-valid read-only history grant can read the compact expired status, release active capacity and the activity lease, and fence the old epoch. The compact tombstone enters the bounded inactive pool, sharing the 1,024 per-project inactive record cap and global disk cap with terminal records but remaining explicitly nonterminal. It is reclaimable under pressure and expires at seven days at most. If the tombstone cannot be retained, delete the inactive record after fencing, make the old task unavailable, and never recreate it from an old callback. A late owner can only enter through a new trusted admission and fresh identity after expiry. A storage fault fails observation closed and remains visible while the expiry transition retries. Grant records have bounded count and encoded size within the same per-task reservation, with expiration and revocation garbage-collected before minting replacements.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: Cursor binds to task, attempt and committed observation revision. In-memory bounded feed resumes at the cursor when available; after gaps or restart use the latest snapshot and explicit resync. Durable milestones record measured changes rather than heartbeat events. Recovery deadline, inactive disposition, expiry reason, scoped grant digests/revocation generation and reserved bytes are persisted. Raw grant secrets and runtime handles never enter the record.

dataModelChanges.entity: Runtime activity and fallback observer leases
dataModelChanges.details: An active attempt can hold at most one activity association to its originating insrc chat, and one chat can hold many associations. Only verified owner activity renews it. The current chat owner can read the scoped retention projection; the adapter and existing client status projection remain s5. Separately, a stable task has at most one fallback scheduling lease across attempts and any number of bounded native observers. Use monotonic slot and lease deadlines while alive and suspend fallback at daemon restart. Persist no scheduler credentials. On restart emit interrupted or unknown until the actual owner revalidates, mint a new owner epoch before accepting further events, and never auto-start work. Persisted terminal state remains authoritative. Conversation removal releases only that association and retains authorized project-scoped results. A lease is valid only while the same current attempt owns its verified runtime epoch. Renewal after 120-second expiry requires new trusted revalidation and a fresh epoch within the recovery window. A 30-second heartbeat is scheduling intent and grants no right to renew from a reader. Fallback leases have a separate 120-second holder lifetime and slot fence. Their live credentials and monotonic timestamps are process-local.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: Lease epoch, holder binding, monotonic schedule anchor, last slot, in-flight slot and cursor. Retention projection exposes task and expiry, not owner credentials.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Provide the common generic delegate, task identity and verified owner-fence invariants. Concrete executors and their detail schemas remain sibling-owned. Predecessor traceability deliverable for ac5: July S001 / #42 → s1 and s2. Common daemon progress, compatible IPC and workflow/analyze producer measurements. July S002 / #43 → s6. MCP progress-token gating, native CLI qualification and optional observation. July S003 / #44 → s5. Typed IDE consumption and terminal progress in current VS Code chat. Each original issue and local story record remains traceable. This crosswalk records coverage only. Tracker linkage and retirement remain a separate decision.

Normalize, persist and authorize snapshots, subscription cursors, fallback schedule and explicit control. Additive IPC routing and authorization belong here; MCP/VS Code presentation belong to their own stories.
Provide verified owner renewal and the read-only association projection. Native clients and the extension session adapter remain outside this story.

errorCases.detection: Trusted server binding fails project, invocation and current-attempt permission checks.
errorCases.response: Return task-unavailable with identical missing/unauthorized shape. Do not consult delegate or emit detail.

errorCases.detection: Owner handle, epoch, sequence, detail schema or serialized-size check fails, including after asynchronous refresh.
errorCases.response: Drop stale writes and preserve last verified measurement with stale or unavailable freshness if source is invalid. Never advance ownership or progress.

errorCases.scenario: Disk commit or capacity reservation fails
errorCases.detection: Write, fsync, rename, validation or reserved-budget check fails.
errorCases.response: Do not publish an uncommitted terminal result. Mark observation degraded, preserve the old committed record, and reconcile against the same owner after recovery. Distinguish failures after rename by re-reading and verifying the durable record before retry.
errorCases.userImpact: Execution continues and can be inspected through its existing result path where available.

errorCases.detection: Startup rehydrates valid envelopes with an owner epoch from a prior process.
errorCases.response: Retain the last verified measurement, mark interrupted or unknown, and fence previous callbacks. Resume observation only after owner proves survival or actual resumption. Preserve terminal state and reconcile pending cancellation without auto-dispatch.
errorCases.userImpact: A restart does not imply completion or relaunch.

errorCases.detection: Rate limit, expired lease, duplicate slot or disconnected holder.
errorCases.response: Publish suspended observation and preserve the shared cadence anchor when a supported holder recovers. Honor retry-after as degraded behavior and avoid overlapping calls or replay bursts.
errorCases.userImpact: Progress may be delayed and is visibly degraded.

errorCases.detection: The persisted recovery deadline expires without trusted survival evidence.
errorCases.response: Persist an expired observation, release its active reservation and retention, reject old epoch, and reclaim the bounded tombstone on pressure or TTL.
errorCases.userImpact: Capacity becomes available while the execution outcome remains unknown.

edgeCases.input: Heartbeat or repeated reads with equal measured progress
edgeCases.expected: Only owner activity and freshness can change. Keep the same meaningful revision and original measurement age.

edgeCases.input: Two authorized viewers, a lagged cursor, and terminal outcome during a full queue
edgeCases.expected: One fallback scheduler at most. Coalesce and explicitly resync lagged observers. Terminal delivery uses reserved capacity and has one stable outcome.

edgeCases.input: Older owner callback arrives after a newer attempt or task terminal
edgeCases.expected: Reject by attempt and epoch, never resurrect retention or overwrite a terminal state.

edgeCases.input: Stop updates races with cancel or normal completion
edgeCases.expected: Detach only the observer. Explicit cancellation is pending until the verified outcome, and request replay cannot duplicate the side effect.

edgeCases.input: Fallback holder disconnects during an accepted poll and a new observer claims the lease
edgeCases.expected: The old generation cannot deliver or advance the cursor. The successor inherits the cadence anchor and slot watermark, with no overlapping admission or catch-up.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Daemon owns state and scope. Keep typed Unix IPC and existing terminal execution semantics.
Existing review trackers and session pool remain authoritative for their own evidence. Observation does not invoke models, alter workflows or imply native-session activity.

migration.stateBefore: Existing IPC dispatch, review checkpoints and ChatSessionPool remain separate sources, as grounded in s1 context. There is no shared durable progress record.
migration.stateAfter: Daemon owns an additive bounded progress record and authorized observation contract. Existing executors and clients continue to work before sibling adapters are connected.

migrationSteps.action: Initialize the private versioned observation namespace on first daemon start. Existing state remains untouched.
Expose the additive foundation to registered consumers and validate recovery, lease fencing and fail-open execution using fixtures.
On rollback remove the additive observation surface and leave its bounded records inert for a later compatible upgrade. Existing executor results and session records remain authoritative.

migration.backwardCompat: The Unix IPC protocol, current review checkpoints, executor outcomes and native session ownership are preserved. Old clients can ignore the additive surface.

alternativesConsidered.name: Atomic bounded record per task
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: One per-task record is the recovery authority for observation state.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Store one versioned envelope per task under the daemon state root, with a reserved bounded record budget. Serialize updates for a task, commit terminal state before publication, and rebuild in-memory cursors and expiry queues from the persisted records on startup.
pros: No cross-file transaction is needed for an attempt transition, current snapshot and retained milestones.
Recovery enumerates at most the reserved capacity and needs no event replay.
cons: A persisted update replaces the bounded record and needs explicit write coalescing.

alternativesConsidered.name: Split snapshot and bounded milestone journal
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Maintain separate bounded checkpoint and milestone files per task.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep a compact current snapshot file plus a capped append journal for meaningful milestones. A shared revision lets recovery discard a journal suffix that was not committed with the snapshot.
pros: Milestones can be appended without rewriting earlier milestone contents.
cons: Snapshot and journal require two-file recovery and can lose otherwise valid suffixes after a crash.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: A split journal needs an additional recovery protocol to keep the snapshot and history consistent.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: The coordinator verifies execution authority before committing a snapshot. Restart recovers the last committed state and never infers live ownership or relaunches work.

participants.label: Executor owner
participants.description: Sends verified facts and owns execution.

participants.label: Coordinator
participants.description: Verifies scope, attempts and owner epochs.

messages.label: Register before detach
messages.description: Bind trusted origin and reserve the bounded record.

messages.label: Commit attempt and fence
messages.description: Persist the current attempt before admitting observation.

messages.label: Read or subscribe with cursor
messages.description: Authorize caller and resolve the task binding.

messages.label: Return snapshot or resync
messages.description: Use the same sanitized snapshot model for every observer.

messages.label: Confirm terminal outcome
messages.description: Reject stale owner epochs and publish no unverified result.

messages.label: Commit terminal snapshot
messages.description: Finish the durable write before notifying readers.

messages.label: Deliver terminal snapshot
messages.description: Use reserved terminal capacity and keep execution outcome stable.

messages.label: Load records after restart
messages.description: Recover only validated committed snapshots and receipts.

messages.label: Reattach after restart
messages.description: Authorize again. Active execution stays unknown or interrupted until reverified.

messages.label: Revalidate a surviving attempt
messages.description: Mint a new epoch before further progress or retention updates.
